chapter: Chicago, Detroit and Seattle Harmony Kings
title: The Lorraine Hotel, one-nighters, and Joe Hooven
summary: He lives by the Loop's elevated train, fakes hot parts on pickup jobs and teams up with trumpeter Joe Hooven.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: They handled some very big - some very big things were handled through the Benson Office. And, I did get some work; I got enough work to get a place to stay and, uh, I stayed in a hotel there called -- I had the hotel in mind yesterday -- "The Lorraine Hotel" -- and that was--- it was on one of the side streets; I remember, my room was right where the elevator train went by -- oh, boy---
This was South Chicago - wasn't it?
No, it was right in the loop.
Was it in the loop area?
Yeah - of course, you know the loop is--- the elevator train runs around the loop so it went right by my hotel window.
Then that was on the South end of the loop then - if you will - right?

Yeah. So, uh, of course, I got to meet a lot of musicians and I worked with a lot of musicians and, you know, when they send you out on these bands, you never knew whether you were going to be a trio or a quartet or ten men or fifteen---
You never knew until you got there---
You never knew until you got there and most of it was - if you were playing the hot trumpet part, you were safe; you could fake your way through some of the arrangements and play the jazz parts.
And, that was primarily what you did---

That's primarily what I did. And, I got by fine on that. And, I met - during that time - I met a wonderful trumpet player named Joe Hooven and we sort of -- he was great reader and player and, uh, we worked out some nice little things together when we worked together, you know - and, so, we were kind of like a team.
You were 20 years old now -- I'm just throwing that in---
